gen-gf-baumans-gf-tajawal: Baumans draws every stroke at a single thickness, with a c like a crescent wrench. Tajawal is a low-key sans-serif beneath it, its c a broad open hook, and that unfussy softness is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-tasa-explorer: Round bowls that look like bent glass tubing mark Baumans. TASA Explorer, a sans-serif with curves that stop like brush strokes lifted early, gives that stiff display face a friendly, approachable partner.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-tasa-orbiter: Wire-bent and wrench-sharp, Baumans looks like cable shaped into letters. Give TASA Orbiter, a sans-serif with unclogged small counters, a modest size, and it stays crisp and professional under that heading.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-teachers: Teachers brings thin steel rod letters whose ink strokes taper out before touching, giving the sans a modern feel. And Baumans, drawn at one thickness with a crescent-wrench c, supplies the commanding display voice above it.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-telex: Telex is curvy and unclamped, a neutral sans-serif with a loose build. If Baumans were made small, its pipe-cleaner-slim joins would lose the commanding presence that sets it apart from that body.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-tenor-sans: Round, mechanical, and a bit stubborn: that is Baumans. And Tenor Sans, with c tips that never creep toward touching, adds faint nib-pressure variation that makes the pair's strongest quality its contrast between hard line and soft pen.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-tirra: Tirra's round forms read like open parentheses, quiet and modern. Baumans stitches its strokes like thread along a path and commands attention, while Tirra, a sans-serif, simply keeps the text moving.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-titillium-web: Approachable, first of all, thanks to Titillium Web and its far-apart stroke ends. Under Baumans, with its single line weight and display swagger, that sans-serif body would carry a long passage without any strain.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-tomorrow: A c like a crescent wrench opened wide gives Baumans its true monoline look. Tomorrow, a plain sans with bowls like a cupped palm of clay, does the quiet work that the display face leaves alone.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-trispace: Trispace sets its letters sparse and wide, with curves opening outward instead of curling in. And Baumans, whose diagonals carry the same heft as its stems, gives the headline punch while that plain sans handles the reading.
